neighbours.label: French-speaking places outside France: Louisiana and its Cajun/Creole country, Quebec and Montreal, Belgium, French-speaking Switzerland, Lebanon and Haiti; France itself, West Africa and non-French-speaking neighbours in the same frames stay low
fire: Every spring, crawfish boils pack the backyards of Breaux Bridge, Louisiana.
Zydeco bands played late into the night at the dance hall in Opelousas.
Snow had already buried the narrow streets of Old Quebec by November.
Commuters in Montreal grumbled about the metro shutdown on Monday.
Tourists in Brussels queued for waffles near the Grand-Place.
Students at the university in Lausanne staged a climate sit-in.
The bakeries of Beirut reopened slowly after the blast.
Election posters covered the walls of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, last week.
quiet: Every spring, barbecue smoke fills the backyards of Lockhart, Texas.
Bluegrass bands played late into the night at the dance hall in Asheville.
Snow had already buried the narrow streets of old Lyon by November.
Commuters in Toronto grumbled about the subway shutdown on Monday.
Tourists in Amsterdam queued for fries near Dam Square.
Students at the university in Zurich staged a climate sit-in.
The bakeries of Marseille reopened slowly after the strike.
Election posters covered the walls of Dakar, Senegal, last week.

notes: Coverage follow-up (new label, reason written in concept-maps/COVERAGE.md before this test): the held Louisiana label (#362 line, coverage #1037) covered 6/16; the misses were Haiti, Montreal, Belgium, Lebanon, Hariri, EPFL. Exploration probes (two rounds, 24 sentences, none reused here) found Senegal, Ivory Coast and Martinique low, so West Africa is a near miss, not a claim.
